entries.title: II Corinthians 12:1
segments: ¶Well, it is not of profit to me to boast, for I will come to visions and revelations of [the] Lord.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:2
segments: I know a man in Christ, fourteen years ago, (whether in [the] body I know not, or out of the body I know not, God knows;) such [a one] caught up to [the] third heaven.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:3
segments: And I know such a man, (whether in [the] body or out of the body I know not, God knows;)

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:4
segments: that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable things said which it is not allowed to man to utter.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:5
segments: Of such [a one] I will boast, but of myself I will not boast, unless in my weaknesses.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:6
segments: For if I shall desire to boast, I shall not be a fool; for I will say [the] truth; but I forbear, lest any one should think as to me above what he sees me [to be], or whatever he may hear of me.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:7
segments: And that I might not be exalted by the exceeding greatness of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn for the flesh, a messenger of Satan that he might buffet me, that I might not be exalted.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:8
segments: For this I thrice besought the Lord that it might depart from me.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:9
segments: And he said to me, My grace suffices thee; for [my] power is perfected in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather boast in my weaknesses, that the power of the Christ may dwell upon me.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:10
segments: Wherefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in insults, in necessities, in persecutions, in straits, for Christ: for when I am weak, then I am powerful.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:11
segments: ¶I have become a fool; *ye* have compelled me; for *I* ought to have been commended by you; for I have been nothing behind those who were in surpassing degree apostles, if also I am nothing.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:12
segments: The signs indeed of the apostle were wrought among you in all endurance, signs, and wonders, and works of power.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:13
segments: For in what is it that ye have been inferior to the other assemblies, unless that I myself have not been in laziness a charge upon you? Forgive me this injury.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:14
segments: Behold, this third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be in laziness a charge; for I do not seek yours, but you; for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:15
segments: Now *I* shall most gladly spend and be utterly spent for your souls, if even in abundantly loving you I should be less loved.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:16
segments: But be it so. *I* did not burden you, but being crafty I took you by guile.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:17
segments: Did I make gain of you by any of those whom I have sent to you?

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:18
segments: I begged Titus, and sent the brother with [him]: did Titus at all make gain of you? have we not walked in the same spirit? [have we] not in the same steps?

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:19
segments: Ye have long been supposing that we excuse ourselves to you: we speak before God in Christ; and all things, beloved, for your building up.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:20
segments: For I fear lest perhaps coming I find you not such as I wish, and that *I* be found by you such as ye do not wish: lest [there might be] strifes, jealousies, angers, contentions, evil speakings, whisperings, puffings up, disturbances;

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:21
segments: lest my God should humble me as to you when I come again, and that I shall grieve over many of those who have sinned before, and have not repented as to the uncleanness and fornication and licentiousness which they have practised.
